key_insight: A flow-based generative model can learn a practical approximation of the invariant phase-space distribution of turbulent channel flow, enabling both synthetic turbulence generation and flow reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven route to create physically consistent turbulent inflow fields and missing-data reconstructions for CFD, reducing reliance on ad hoc synthetic turbulence models.
method: Train a flow-based generative model on a minimal conditional flow unit for turbulent channel flow at Reτ=180.
Define a consistent conditional sampling procedure so fields conditioned on a center observation can be sampled coherently.
Test whether generated fields preserve physical statistics and dynamical invariance, including use as DNS initial conditions.
evidence_signal: Direct numerical simulation comparisons show the learned samples reproduce key turbulent statistics and dynamics, including intermittency, nonlinear energy transfer, and stationary ensemble behavior when used in DNS.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated for channel flow at Reτ=180, so generalization to other Reynolds numbers, geometries, and sparse-observation settings still needs validation.
paper_title: A machine-learned probability distribution in the phase space of turbulent channel flow for synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction
